model_output:
To transpose a text in Python, you can use the `str.swapcase()` method, which allows you to swap the case of characters in a string. Here's an example of how you could use it:
```
text = "Hello, World!"
transposed_text = text.swapcase()
print(transposed_text)
```
This will output `"!dlroW ,olleH"`, which is the original text with the case of each letter swapped.

Alternatively, you could use the `str.lower()` and `str.upper()` methods to manually transpose the text. For example:
```
text = "Hello, World!"
transposed_text = text.lower() + text.upper()
print(transposed_text)
```
This will also output `"!dlroW ,olleH"`, but it requires more code and is less efficient than using the `swapcase()` method.
